scope: Two native clients (no emulator; Linux, or the Windows exe under Wine) through the native C bridge, unchanged companions, the real world server and the launcher's trade-capable ownership store: both legacy saves enrolled through the running games; A opens Start > Player > Players, picks B, Trade Pokemon and its first eligible Pokemon; B opens Pending trade and offers its first; both screens show both offers; A's confirmation alone commits nothing; B's completes it (revision 3 on both, ownership conserved: the parties' serials are exchanged, none lost or doubled; each running game's party in memory equals its new canonical save); A starts another trade and backs out with B (aborted, nothing moves); both games closed and started again from closed-game recovery hold the parties of their latest canonical saves; host store integrity; source saves unchanged. Ordinary key presses on each game's own X display; the harness reads the games' memory (/proc/PID/mem at the non-PIE executable's symbols) only to see the menus and compare parties.
